# PROCESS — cand_0001 (empty seed → first capability)

Starting state: prompt.md empty (no system message), no task_template.md (adapter built-in template, which ends "once that file exists, you are done"). Val 0.450 (18/40). No environment faults found: every trace executed code, and each failure has a task-level cause.

Grader fact verified in the trace score blobs: `reward_metric: hard_no_recalc`. Seven tasks have `test_case_results=[1]` but `test_case_results_no_recalc=[0]`, so they are correct once recalculated and fail only because they wrote formulas.

## Ranked issue list
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula written instead of value (grader doesn't recalc) | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942, 55979, 56563, 9569, 53647, 54144, 37456 (+267-18 edited formula text) | "How do I write a formula…" is answered by writing a formula string; it reads back empty or as error text | KNOWLEDGE / CONTRACT | output contract + reason (prompt.md) |
| 2 | B. No inspection: coordinates taken from the pandas preview (row off by one), layout/axes/examples ignored | 227-40, 59196, 50768, 53647, 39046, 43436, 48527 | acts in round 1 without reading real cells; preview index 0 = Excel row 2 | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure step 1 (template) + knowledge line on the preview offset + "reproduce examples" rule |
| 3 | C. pandas to_excel rewrite clobbers sheet/other cells | 227-40, 48527, 50768, 80-42, 39046 | round-trips the whole sheet | KNOWLEDGE (method) | concrete openpyxl idiom (prompt.md) |
| 4 | D. No verification, 30-round resubmit loop | 51-12, 53647, 54144, 9569, 80-42, 227-40, 39046, 43436 (also many passing tasks loop harmlessly) | built-in template: "once that file exists, you are done" but no way to finish is stated; agent resends the same code | STRUCTURE | template steps 3–4: verify by printing answer_position, then finish with a no-code reply |
| 5 | E. Pre-filled example / correct cells in the target overwritten | 48527, 39046, 54144 | treats the whole range as blank | CONTRACT | "keep cells that are already correct; examples are part of expected" |
| 6 | F. Float threshold comparison | 51-12 | 100*1.1 ≠ 110 | KNOWLEDGE | one tolerance line |
| 7 | G. Formula-cell text edited instead of displayed value | 267-18 | loaded without data_only | KNOWLEDGE | data_only read / normal write idiom |

## Changes made
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | tighten output contract + reason | prompt.md "How your output is graded" | grader reads stored values → compute a formula's result and write the literal; applies to every "create a formula" task | all 18 passing tasks already write literals (they pass no_recalc) |
| A/E/type | contract | prompt.md | literal types, exact source spelling; keep correct pre-filled cells | passing tasks already comply |
| C/G | knowledge (method) | prompt.md "Working with the workbook" | openpyxl load→set→save, data_only second copy, no to_excel | passing pandas tasks (e.g. 31628) write the same values; openpyxl preserves more, so it changes the method but not the graded values |
| B | knowledge + restructure | prompt.md + template step 1 | preview offset stated; inspect real cells before solving; examples must be reproduced | passing tasks gain one inspection round; they have ≥25 rounds spare |
| D | ordered procedure | task_template.md steps 1–4 | replaces "once that file exists, you are done" with inspect → solve → verify → finish (no code block) | adapter stops on a no-code reply once the answer exists, so passing tasks end earlier with the same file |
| F | knowledge | prompt.md | float tolerance idiom | only affects threshold comparisons |
| literal-instruction | rule | prompt.md | "append after existing data even if it looks done" (80-42) | bounded to append tasks |

## Verify-the-fix
- trace 46897/55049/9569/56563…: final code `ws['I3'] = '=COUNTIF(...)'`; feedback says "answer cells hold FORMULAS". The new contract says a "how do I write a formula" task expects the value, and to compute it in Python. 9569's own debug helper `get_earliest_value` already computed the right values.
- trace 59196/53647/227-40: hardcoded rows taken from the preview (header on row 2 / C4 vs C5 / iloc[13] = row 15). Step 1 now requires printing real openpyxl addresses before solving, and prompt.md states the index-0 = row 2 offset (checked against the adapter: `read_excel` default header, extent reported as `rows 1-{nrows+1}`).
- trace 39046/48527/43436/50768: the example cells F2:F4, D2 "Apple", column H, and F14 went unread. Step 1 prints them, and the rule says to reproduce the examples before filling the rest.
- trace 51-12/54144: the same code was sent about 28 times until round 30, with no print. Step 3 prints answer_position; step 4 names the exit (plain-text reply). The adapter code confirms a no-code reply ends the loop once solution_code exists.
- trace 267-18: `//=CONCATENATE(` written. The data_only rule means the displayed value gets edited instead.
- trace 80-42: pandas ExcelWriter rewrite, and the agent decided "already consolidated". The openpyxl idiom and the literal-instruction rule address both.
- Template placeholder contract validated with the adapter's `_task_template_error` → None, and it renders.

## Process & features used
- 3 parallel read-only diagnosis subagents (5 traces each). I read the formula cluster and a passing 30-round trace myself.
- No prior iterations exist (RUNMAP is empty; rejected.jsonl is empty).

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The literal-values contract, the openpyxl edit idiom, and the verify-then-finish-with-no-code procedure.

## Deliberately skipped
- 43436's month-end boundary semantics (ambiguous; needs gold). 80-42 is a large consolidation task, and only the general rules are applied to it.
- Excel-365 function lists: moot once values are computed in Python.
